Part of the 17 Media group, which lists in Japan, with offices across Asia. Funding of about $160 million shown. Consumer-facing app with high awareness in Japan and Taiwan, mostly among young viewers and streamers.

Professional networking site and recruiting platform, founded in 2002, with over a billion members. Revenue comes from recruiting products, premium subscriptions, learning and advertising. Acquired by Microsoft in December 2016 for about $26 billion and operating as a Microsoft subsidiary, with its main offices in Sunnyvale, California. Funding of about $155 million shown reflects its earlier private rounds. One of the best-known professional brands, widely recognised by workers and employers globally.

Trackforce Valiant provides software for the private security guarding industry, with mobile apps and a workforce platform for scheduling, guard tours, incident reporting and payroll. It was formed through the combination of Trackforce and Valiant, backed by private equity, with $150 million raised in September 2019. Customers are security guard companies and facilities that employ patrol officers, mainly in North America. It earns subscription software fees. Based in Southlake, Texas. B2B enterprise software with little consumer visibility, so limited sponsorship appeal beyond corporate hospitality.

about: Nerdy is a US online learning company behind the Varsity Tutors brand, offering live one-to-one and group tutoring, test preparation and AI-assisted learning tools. It sells to families directly and to schools and districts, plus an enterprise segment, earning session and subscription revenue. Headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, and founded as Varsity Tutors in 2007. It went public via a SPAC merger in 2021 and trades on the NYSE under NRDY, with annual revenue near $190 million. Recognizable US education consumer brand with national advertising, but modest global profile.

Matrimony.com is an Indian online matchmaking and wedding services company based in Chennai, founded in 2000 by Murugavel Janakiraman. It runs BharatMatrimony and more than a dozen community matrimony sites, EliteMatrimony for premium users, and Assisted Service with offline centres, plus a wedding services marketplace. Customers are Indian families and diaspora users who pay subscription fees for paid memberships. It is listed on the NSE and BSE under MATRIMONY, with revenue around INR 4.5 billion. Very high brand recognition among Indian consumers and a heavy advertiser.

Clavister is a Swedish cybersecurity company based in Ornskoldsvik, founded in 1997, that builds network security software and firewalls under the cOS Core and cOS Stream names. It sells to telecom operators, managed security service providers, governments and enterprises, and since 2020s increasingly to defence and military vehicle makers through its onWire and Defence Grade products, with Swedish and European customers. It is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm under CLAV. Crunchbase shows about $39 million in funding. B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

Tokens.com is a Canadian digital asset company based in Toronto that invests in and operates Web3 businesses, including metaverse real estate, NFTs and its Metaverse Group subsidiary, as well as cryptocurrency staking activities. It earns income from staking, investments and digital asset sales, serving crypto investors rather than consumers directly. It is listed on the Canadian NEO Exchange and OTC markets under COIN. Crunchbase shows about $38 million in funding, latest in October 2021. Visible in crypto media but a small company with limited mainstream awareness.

Naga is a German fintech and social trading group based in Hamburg, offering the NAGA trading app and platform where retail customers trade CFDs, stocks and crypto and copy other traders' portfolios, plus a Visa card and wallet. It earns trading spreads, fees and card income, serving retail clients in Europe, Asia and elsewhere, and is regulated through licences in Cyprus and Seychelles. The parent, The NAGA Group AG, is listed in Frankfurt under N4G. Crunchbase shows about $38 million in funding. Online brand with moderate consumer awareness in Europe.

WildBlue Communications was a US satellite broadband provider, founded in 2001 and based in Colorado, offering high-speed satellite internet to rural households and small businesses in the US, using Ka-band capacity from Telesat and its own satellites. It was acquired by ViaSat in late 2009 for about $568 million and later rebranded as Exede, now Viasat internet. Crunchbase shows $693 million in funding by 2008. No longer an independent brand.

about: Zain Group is a Kuwait-based mobile telecoms group with operations in Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Jordan, Bahrain and Sudan, serving about 50 million customers with voice, data, fibre, 5G and enterprise services. It started as MTC in Kuwait and later expanded across Africa, then sold African businesses. Listed on the Boursa Kuwait (ZAIN), with large shareholders including Kuwait's Public Institution for Social Security. Strong consumer brand across the Gulf and a prominent sports and events sponsor in the region.

Calient Technologies is a US optical networking company based in Santa Barbara, California, that makes MEMS-based optical circuit switches used in data centres and telecom networks for fast reconfigurable fibre connections. Customers are cloud providers, telecoms and research networks. It is privately held and venture backed. Crunchbase shows about $535 million in total funding by August 2019. B2B hardware company with no consumer profile.

Listed on SIX Swiss Exchange (DOKA). B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

Transinfo Group (Beijing Transinfo Technology) is a Chinese independent provider of intelligent transportation systems, urban rail and public transport data, software and IT services, based in Beijing, selling to metro operators, transport authorities and city governments. about: United Internet is a German internet services group based in Montabaur, founded in 1988 by Ralph Dommermuth, who remains its largest shareholder. Its brands include 1&1 (mobile and broadband), IONOS (cloud hosting and web), GMX, WEB.DE (consumer email) and Strato. Customers are millions of consumers and small businesses in Germany and Europe, with revenue of about EUR 6 billion. Listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (UTDI). Consumer brands are household names in Germany.

Actifio was a US data management company based in Waltham, Massachusetts, whose copy data management platform let enterprises back up, recover and reuse production data across on-premises and cloud systems. Customers were large enterprises and service providers. It raised about $392 million and was acquired by Google Cloud in late 2020. It is no longer independent. B2B enterprise software, with no consumer awareness.

Apttus was a US software company, based in San Mateo, California, that sold cloud applications for configure, price, quote (CPQ), contract management and revenue lifecycle on Salesforce. B2B enterprise software, no consumer awareness.

It is privately owned and raised about $412 million as shown by Crunchbase in 2015. B2B brand, widely known in financial research circles.

iFlytek is a Chinese artificial intelligence company based in Hefei, Anhui, founded in 1999 as a spin-off from the University of Science and Technology of China. Customers include schools, governments, carmakers and consumers, with revenue above RMB 20 billion. Listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (002230) and on the US export control list since 2019. High domestic brand awareness.

Marigold is a US marketing technology company, based in Nashville, Tennessee, created in 2021 from the combination of Campaign Monitor, Cheetah Digital, Sailthru and others by CM Group. Funding shown is $410 million since 2019. B2B software with little consumer awareness.

Contentful is a German software company, based in Berlin and with a large US presence in San Francisco, that sells a composable content platform, a headless content management system for building websites, apps and digital products. Customers include large retailers, media and enterprises, paying subscription fees. Founded in 2013, it raised about $350 million and was valued at $3 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B software brand, with no consumer awareness.

Infinidat is an enterprise data storage company founded in 2011 by Moshe Yanai, based in Waltham, Massachusetts with a large Israeli R&D centre, selling InfiniBox and InfiniGuard storage and ransomware-resistant data protection to large enterprises and service providers. It is private and has raised about $370 million. Customers include telecoms and financial firms. B2B hardware and software brand with no consumer awareness.

Iterable is a US cross-channel marketing automation platform, based in San Francisco, used by brands to send personalised email, push, SMS and in-app messages, with AI tools for optimisation. Customers are consumer brands and retailers, paying subscription fees, and the company raised about $342 million, with a $2 billion valuation in 2021. Founded in 2013. B2B software, with no consumer awareness.

Jamf is a US software company, based in Minneapolis, that makes tools for managing, securing and deploying Apple devices (Macs, iPhones, iPads) in schools and enterprises. It listed on Nasdaq (JAMF) in 2020 after backing from Vista Equity Partners, and in 2025 Francisco Partners agreed to acquire it in a take-private deal worth about $2.2 billion. Revenue was around $600 million. B2B IT brand with no consumer awareness.

LaunchDarkly is a US software company, based in Oakland, California, whose feature management platform lets engineering teams release, toggle and test software features safely, with experimentation and AI model configuration tools. Customers are thousands of software companies and enterprises, paying subscription fees. Founded in 2014, it raised about $330 million and was valued near $3 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B developer brand, with no consumer awareness.

Molo Finance is a UK digital mortgage platform, based in London, that uses technology to help homebuyers and borrowers apply for mortgages faster, mixing automated underwriting with advice. Customers are UK borrowers, and funding of around 270 million, much of it likely debt, is shown by October 2020. A small challenger in a market dominated by banks. about: PatSnap is an intellectual property and innovation intelligence software company, founded in China in 2007 and operating from Singapore, with offices in Shenzhen, the US and Europe. It raised about $350 million, including a $300 million Series E in 2021. B2B software with no consumer awareness.

Qumulo is a US enterprise file storage software company, based in Seattle, founded in 2012, whose scale-out file data platform runs on-premises and in public clouds for media, healthcare, research and government customers. It sells subscriptions and raised about $347 million. Privately held. B2B software brand with no consumer awareness.

Redis is a US data technology company, based in Mountain View, California, which commercialises the open-source Redis in-memory database, used for caching, real-time data and AI applications, through Redis Cloud and Redis Enterprise. Customers are developers and enterprises, including large internet companies. It has raised about $357 million, valued at $2 billion in 2021, and has changed its licence several times. B2B developer brand, widely known among software engineers.

SnapLogic is a US enterprise software company, based in San Mateo, California, founded in 2006 by Gaurav Dhillon, whose integration platform as a service (iPaaS) connects applications, data and APIs with a low-code interface and AI agents. Customers are large enterprises, paying subscription fees. It raised about $371 million, including a $165 million round in 2021. Privately held. B2B software, with no consumer awareness.

Unqork is a US no-code enterprise application platform, based in New York, founded in 2017 by Gary Hoberman. It lets banks, insurers and governments build complex software with visual tools rather than hand-written code. Customers include large financial firms and public agencies, paying subscriptions. It raised about $365 million, with a valuation of $2 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B software, no consumer awareness.

Vectra AI is a US cybersecurity company, based in San Jose, California, founded in 2011, whose platform uses AI to detect and prioritise attacks across networks, cloud, identity and SaaS (the Attack Signal Intelligence approach). Customers are large enterprises and government agencies, with revenue from subscriptions. It raised about $353 million and was valued at $1.2 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

Workfront was a US enterprise work management software company, based in Lehi, Utah, whose cloud platform helped marketing and creative teams plan and track projects. Customers were large enterprises. Adobe acquired Workfront in December 2020 for about $1.5 billion and it is now part of Adobe Experience Cloud. It raised about $375 million before that. B2B software, no consumer awareness.
